Per-Unit Systems and Multi-Island Handling

Two essential topics for real-world power systems: unit conversion and topology handling.

Per-Unit Conversion System

Problem: Solvers use dimensionless per-unit values. Users think in physical units (MW, kV).

Solution: Convert on input, store coefficients, convert back on output.

Why Per-Unit?

1. Better conditioned equations

  • Raw physical: 500 MW vs 1.05 pu voltage (many orders of magnitude)
  • Per-unit: 0.5 pu power vs 1.05 pu voltage (similar scales)
  • Newton solver performs better

2. Portable parameters

  • 0.05 pu reactance same behavior at any voltage level
  • 13.8 kV transformer vs 230 kV transformer - same pu value
  • Captures device essence independent of physical scale

3. User-friendly reports

  • Compute in pu (numerical stability)
  • Report in physical (user understanding)
  • "Bus 4 voltage is 142.0 kV" better than "1.03 pu"

Three-Part Storage

1. sys.models - Per-unit values (for computation)

sys.models.PQ.pl[3]  # → 0.478 pu (on system base)
  • Used by residual calculations
  • Newton solver never sees physical units

2. sys.parsed_data - Original physical values (optional)

sys.parsed_data.models.PQ.pl[3]  # → 47.8 MW (from file)
  • Data provenance
  • Debugging
  • Only if you pass parsed_data during construction

3. sys.pu_coeffs - Conversion coefficients

sys.pu_coeffs.PQ.pl[3]  # → 100.0 (system base MVA)
  • Per-instance coefficients
  • Enables exact inverse conversion
  • Physical = pu × coefficient

Metadata-Driven Conversion

Models declare what needs conversion:

const PQ_PARAMS = [
    ModelParam(:pl, PowerNominal, description="Constant power P", units="MW"),
    ModelParam(:ql, PowerNominal, description="Constant power Q", units="MVAR"),
    ModelParam(:yp, AdmittanceNominal, description="Constant admittance P", units="MW"),
]

PUType determines conversion formula:

  • PowerNominal - Divide by system base MVA
  • AdmittanceNominal - Use voltage base² / power base
  • VoltageNominal - Divide by base kV
  • ImpedanceNominal - Use voltage base² / power base
  • AngleDegrees - Convert to radians

Example:

# System base: 100 MVA
# Physical: 47.8 MW
# Coefficient: 1/100 = 0.01
# Per-unit: 47.8 × 0.01 = 0.478 pu

External Base Quantities

Some conversions need info from other models:

const PQ_EXT_PARAMS = [
    ExtParam(:basekv, PQ_TERMINALS[1], :basekv, BaseVoltage(), PrePerUnit(),
             required=true, description="Connected bus base voltage"),
]

Retrieval phases:

  • PrePerUnit - Get before conversion (dimensionless, bases)
  • PostPerUnit - Get after conversion (already in pu)

Example: Admittance conversion needs bus base voltage

# System base: 100 MVA, Bus base: 13.8 kV
# Zb = 13.8² / 100 = 1.9044 ohms
# Admittance conversion uses 1/Zb

Conversion Workflow

During SystemModel construction:

1. Build IndexOrder

ext2int(parsed_data)  # External IDs → internal indices

2. Retrieve PrePerUnit parameters

retrieve_external_params(sys, PrePerUnit())
# Gets base voltages, bus types, etc.

3. Calculate coefficients

calc_pu_coefficients(sys)
# For each parameter of each instance
# Uses device ratings + external bases + PUType formula

4. Convert to per-unit

convert_to_per_unit(sys)
# Multiply physical values × coefficients → pu values
# Structural fields (IDs, status) unchanged

5. Retrieve PostPerUnit parameters

retrieve_external_params(sys, PostPerUnit())
# Rare, for quantities needing consistent pu

Result:

  • sys.models - Per-unit (computation)
  • sys.pu_coeffs - Coefficients (reports)
  • sys.parsed_data - Original (provenance)

Inverse Conversion for Reports

Automatic conversion back to physical:

bus_data = collect_model_table(sol, :Bus)
# Returns DataFrame with kV, MW, MVAR, degrees

Process:

  1. Extract pu values from solution
  2. Look up pu_coeffs for each quantity
  3. Multiply: physical = pu × coefficient

Example:

# Per-unit: V_pu = 1.03
# Base: Vb = 138 kV
# Report: 1.03 × 138 = 142.14 kV

Observations use PUType from metadata:

ModelObservation(:p_flow, ActivePower, units="pu", ...)
# ActivePower → multiply by system MVA base → MW

Per-instance coefficients: Not all generators have same MVA rating. Not all buses have same base voltage. Coefficients account for heterogeneity.

Multi-Island Topology

Problem: Networks can disconnect (line outages, planned separations). Each island solves independently.

Island Detection

Uses breadth-first search on network graph:

1. Build graph from Terminal API

# Each model declares terminals
Branch: two terminals (i, j buses)
Load: one terminal (i bus)

# Buses = vertices, devices = edges

2. Find connected components

# Standard graph algorithm
# Each subgraph = one island

3. Identify slack buses per island

# Each island needs exactly one slack bus
# System warns if zero or multiple per island

Result stored in TopologyInfo:

  • Number of islands
  • island_map - Vector assigning each bus to island
  • Slack bus indices per island
  • Adjacency matrix
  • Component lists

Cached in sys.topology for reuse.

Island Splitting

split_islands(sys) extracts disconnected islands:

Single island:

result = split_islands(sys)
# Returns original SystemModel unchanged

Multiple islands:

result = split_islands(sys)
# Returns Vector{SystemModel} (one per island)

Each island is complete independent SystemModel:

  • Own IndexOrder
  • Own address space (when creating ACPowerFlowProblem)
  • Own models collection

Splitting process:

1. Identify buses per island

island_map[bus_idx] → island_number

2. Filter models

# Load at bus 7 → whichever island contains bus 7
# Branch connecting 3-4 → island only if both buses in island

Uses Terminal declarations to determine connectivity.

3. Rebuild index mappings

# Island 2 has buses [5, 7, 11] from original
# External IDs: 5, 7, 11 (unchanged)
# Internal indices: 1, 2, 3 (new, per-island)

4. Re-retrieve external parameters

# Each island runs ext2int → build foreign_refs
# Then retrieve_external_params
# Can't reuse parent's ext_params (internal indices changed)

5. Filter per-unit coefficients

# Parent has entries for all devices
# Island has entries only for its devices
# Coefficient values unchanged (just slice arrays)

Solving Multi-Island Systems

Automatic detection and handling:

prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys)  # Auto-detects islands
sol = solve(prob, NewtonRaphson())  # Solves each independently

Unified variable access:

# Works same for single or multi-island
v = get_var(sol, :Bus, :v, (4001,))
# MultiIslandSolution routes to correct island

User code doesn't change for multi-island cases.

Manual splitting for parallel solving:

result = split_islands(sys)
if result isa Vector
    # Multiple islands - solve in parallel
    solutions = pmap(island -> solve(ACPowerFlowProblem(island), NewtonRaphson()), result)
else
    # Single island
    solution = solve(ACPowerFlowProblem(result), NewtonRaphson())
end

Result type encodes split:

  • SystemModel - Single connected island
  • Vector{SystemModel} - Multiple islands

Contingency Analysis

Simulate component outages:

# Simulate line outage
sys.models.Branch.st[42] = false

# Check topology impact
result = split_islands(sys; auto_analyze=true)
if result isa Vector
    @warn "Contingency creates $(length(result)) islands!"
    for (i, island) in enumerate(result)
        n_buses = length(island.models.Bus)
        println("Island $i: $n_buses buses")
    end
end

# Solve each island for post-contingency state

auto_analyze=true recomputes connectivity with outage in effect.

Island and Per-Unit Interaction

Typical workflow:

  1. Parse data file (physical units)
  2. Convert to per-unit (system base)
  3. Create SystemModel
  4. Split islands if needed

Each island inherits parent's per-unit values and coefficients.

Filtering preserves invariants:

# Parent: Load 3 is 0.478 pu with coefficient 100.0
# Island: Load 3 is 0.478 pu with coefficient 100.0
# Physical: 47.8 MW (same before and after)

Island-specific coefficient storage:

  • Parent has 50 loads → pu_coeffs with 50 entries
  • Island has 12 loads → pu_coeffs with 12 entries
  • Indexing local to island

Reports from island solutions:

# Each island's collect_model_table uses its own pu_coeffs
# Conversion correct (coefficients filtered consistently)

Architecture Implications

Both topics demonstrate key principles:

1. Separation of Data from Computation

  • SystemModel = data (per-unit values, coefficients, topology)
  • ACPowerFlowProblem = computation spec
  • Island splitting creates new SystemModels (data layer)

2. Metadata-Driven Design

  • Per-unit uses model metadata (PARAMS declarations)
  • Island splitting uses Terminal metadata (connectivity)
  • No hardcoded model-specific knowledge

3. Composition Over Special Cases

  • Multi-island = Vector{SystemModel} (not special type)
  • Each island is regular SystemModel
  • Composes with existing problem/solver code

4. Reference-Based Parameters

  • External params flow via references (not duplication)
  • Splitting doesn't copy external params
  • Each island retrieves its own (based on filtered models)

5. Type-Driven Dispatch

  • split_islands returns SystemModel or Vector{SystemModel}
  • Type encodes single vs multi-island
  • User code can dispatch or use unified interface

Patterns extend to other domains:

  • Multi-area coordination → Vector{SystemModel} (regions)
  • Hierarchical systems → Nested SystemModels
  • Same architecture supports different decompositions

Implementation Notes

Adding Models with Per-Unit Conversion

1. Declare params metadata

const MY_MODEL_PARAMS = [
    ModelParam(:power, PowerNominal, description="...", units="MW"),
    ModelParam(:voltage, VoltageNominal, description="...", units="kV"),
    ModelParam(:angle, AngleDegrees, description="...", units="deg"),
]

2. Declare device ratings (if needed)

const MY_MODEL_RATINGS = [
    ModelRating(:mbase, NominalPower, description="Device MVA base"),
]

3. Declare external bases (if needed)

const MY_MODEL_EXT_PARAMS = [
    ExtParam(:basekv, MY_TERMINALS[1], :basekv, BaseVoltage(), PrePerUnit(), ...),
]

4. Test round-trip

# Verify: convert to pu → convert back → matches original

Working with Multi-Island Systems

1. Use Terminal API

# Declare terminals through get_terminals
# Makes model compatible with topology analysis

2. Don't store cross-model references

# Use external IDs, let IndexOrder handle mapping
# Enables filtering without breaking references

3. Test both connected and disconnected

# Verify model works in single and multi-island
# Behavior should be identical (just instance count differs)

4. Handle missing slack buses

# Topology analyzer warns about islands without slack
# Provide clear error messages (not mysterious convergence failure)

Quick Reference

Per-Unit Conversion

# System construction (automatic conversion)
case = PowerFlowData.parse_network("cases/ieee14.raw")
sys = SystemModel(case)  # Converts to pu, stores coefficients

# Access per-unit values
sys.models.PQ.pl[3]  # → 0.478 pu

# Access coefficients
sys.pu_coeffs.PQ.pl[3]  # → 100.0

# Reports (automatic inverse conversion)
df = collect_model_table(sol, :Bus)  # → kV, MW, MVAR, degrees

Multi-Island Handling

# Automatic detection
prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys)  # Detects islands
sol = solve(prob, NewtonRaphson())  # Solves each independently

# Manual splitting
result = split_islands(sys)
if result isa Vector
    # Multiple islands
    for island in result
        prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(island)
        sol = solve(prob, NewtonRaphson())
    end
else
    # Single island
    prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(result)
    sol = solve(prob, NewtonRaphson())
end

# Contingency analysis
sys.models.Branch.st[42] = false  # Outage
result = split_islands(sys; auto_analyze=true)

Common PUTypes

PowerNominal        # MW, MVAR → divide by system MVA base
VoltageNominal      # kV → divide by base kV
ImpedanceNominal    # ohms → use Vb²/Sb
AdmittanceNominal   # Siemens → use Sb/Vb²
AngleDegrees        # deg → convert to radians
Dimensionless       # No conversion
